(a) Effective Date.—Except as otherwise provided in this Act, this Act and the amendments made by this Act shall take effect 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act. 
    (b) Application of Amendments.—
        (1) In general.—Except as otherwise provided in this Act and paragraph (2), the amendments made by this Act shall not apply with respect to cases commenced under title 11, United States Code, before the effective date of this Act. 
        (2) Certain limitations applicable to debtors.—The amendments made by sections 308, 322, and 330 shall apply with respect to cases commenced under title 11, United States Code, on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This section only sets the effective date of the Act and specifies which bankruptcy cases the amendments apply to. The tempting reading is that the reference to "cases commenced under title 11" involves outside parties litigating, but that merely describes the temporal scope of the amendments and does not grant anyone a right to sue over or take part in a federal decision. No outside party is consulted, heard, or otherwise involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: this Act and the amendments made by this Act shall take effect 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act.

qwen_block.w: This section solely defines the effective date and the temporal scope of the amendments. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or comment periods mentioned.
qwen_block.s: (a) Effective Date.—Except as otherwise provided in this Act, this Act and the amendments made by this Act shall take effect 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act.

opus.w: This is an effective-date and applicability provision. It sets when the Act's amendments take effect and which bankruptcy cases they cover. The reference to cases under title 11 only describes which pending litigation the law applies to. It does not let an outside party sue over or object to a federal decision, and it creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory body.
opus.s: the amendments made by this Act shall not apply with respect to cases commenced under title 11, United States Code, before the effective date of this Act.
opus.b: Possible misreading: the mention of "cases commenced under title 11" could look like litigation rights. That fails because the section only sets when the amendments apply to bankruptcy cases. It gives no outside party a right to challenge a federal decision, and no one outside the government takes part in one.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the effective date and applicability of the Act's amendments. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government before a decision is made. The mention of 'debtors' refers to the class of people affected by the law, not participants in the legislative or administrative decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Effective Date.—Except as otherwise provided in this Act, this Act and the amendments made by this Act shall take effect 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the amendments apply to cases involving debtors (who are outside the government), the section involves participation. However, the section merely defines the temporal scope of the law's application (effective dates and retroactivity). It does not establish a process for consultation, comment, hearing, or advisory input from outside parties before a decision is made. It is a procedural provision regarding when the law takes effect, not a mechanism for public participation in decision-making.
